subtitle: Telling inside changes from outside changes, ordering transformations correctly, and choosing the right inverse branch

problems.desc: Part (b): the two values differ, so the claim is false, and the response must say WHY. A correct diagnosis distinguishes the +5 outside f, which adds 5 to the output and shifts the graph up, from the +5 inside f, which changes the input and shifts the graph 5 units left. Naming which one is a vertical shift and which is a horizontal one is the whole answer; saying only that the numbers came out different is a check, not a diagnosis.

traps.desc: shifted up by 1 before stretching, so the stretch doubled the 1 as well

problems.desc: Part (b): a correct diagnosis says that the vertical stretch has to be applied before the vertical shift, because a stretch multiplies whatever is already there. Shifting up 1 first and then stretching by 2 multiplies that 1 and lifts the vertex to a height of 2 instead of 1. The horizontal shift is not the problem and an answer that blames it earns no credit.

Part (b): starting at -4 and coming back at 4 shows the round trip fails, so the response must give the restriction that repairs it: f must be cut down to x at or above 0 before the square root can serve as its inverse. Accept an answer that restricts to x at or below 0 ONLY if it also changes the inverse rule to the negative square root. An answer that merely repeats that the two numbers disagree has diagnosed nothing.

traps.desc: shifted down 4 before stretching, so the stretch tripled the 4

problems.desc: Part (b): Maya applied the two outside operations in the wrong order. Stretching by 3 must come first, giving 3 times the absolute value, and only then is 4 subtracted; her bracket subtracted 4 first and then tripled it, moving the graph down 12 instead of 4. A correct response names the order and says which number got multiplied when it should not have been.

Part (b): the round trip returns 3 rather than -3, which shows the proposed inverse is not undoing f on that input. A correct response states that the outputs of f are never negative, so the inverse rule needs the domain x at or above 0, and that with all real numbers allowed the rule is not the inverse of f at all. Award no credit for changing the formula instead of restricting it.

Part (b): the evidence is that the same height of 4 is reached at 8 instead of 16, so every point has moved to half its former distance from the y-axis. That is a horizontal COMPRESSION by a factor of one half, not a stretch by 2. A correct response uses the two computed inputs as the reason; naming compression with no reference to them is only half the answer.

traps.desc: reflected after adding 5, so the whole shifted graph was negated

problems.desc: Part (b): the minus sign attaches to the squared term only, so the reflection happens before the 5 is added. Reflecting last negates the 5 as well and puts the vertex at a height of -5 instead of 5. A correct response says that a reflection in the x-axis must be applied before any vertical shift, or equivalently that the minus sign in the printed rule does not reach the +5.

traps.desc: kept the plus square root, which inverts the other branch of the parabola

problems.desc: Part (b): completing the square gives a vertex at x equal to 2, and the stated restriction keeps the left branch, where every input is at or below 2. The inverse must therefore return values at or below 2, which forces the minus square root; the plus square root returns values at or above 2 and so inverts the right branch instead. A correct response names the vertex, says which branch the restriction keeps, and connects that to the sign of the root.
